supporting_observations.claim: Seven proxy CONNECT records request update.ledgerlink.com:443 between 13:39:45 and 14:09:24 UTC, at intervals of roughly five minutes.

Network events associate those repeated connections with C:\Program Files\LedgerLink\ledgerlinkupd.exe (PID 3128), running as SUNRIDGE\max.fischer and connecting through the explicit proxy at 10.55.20.30:8080.

The observed destination and cadence match the supplied inventory description of the approved LedgerLink updater checking update.ledgerlink.com about every five minutes, supporting a benign disposition for the alerted activity.

The updater process was recorded as a child of Chrome, an unusual lineage worth noting, but the available records do not show that this caused the repeated updater connections to an unapproved destination.

known_telemetry_limitations: The supplied records show the repeated LedgerLink requests from 13:39:45 onward, but do not show a matching request in the 13:30–13:39 portion of the alert window.

For the updater requests, the proxy records show CONNECT tunnel metadata rather than inspected HTTPS request content; the supplied process events do not provide a binary hash or signature verification. Relevant records: T246-00092, T246-00095, T246-00137, T246-00191, T246-00216, T246-00258, T246-00271, T246-00275.
claims_not_established: The logs do not establish whether the updater binary is authentic, signed, or unchanged; process identity and path are recorded, but no hash or signature result is provided (T246-00092, T246-00093).

The records do not establish a connection between these LedgerLink updater checks and the scheduled svc-ledger password rotation; the observed process is ledgerlinkupd.exe on WS-MFISCHER-01 (T246-00092, T246-00095).
unrelated_findings: Separate review: vpnagent.exe started on WS-MFISCHER-01 despite the supplied environment context stating there is no VPN; these records do not connect it to the alerted LedgerLink traffic (T246-00220, T246-00221).

Separate review: WS-MFISCHER-01 made an SMB connection to FILE-SUN-01, and FILE-SUN-01 recorded an ANONYMOUS LOGON using NTLM. The records do not identify the accessed share or file, and this is not the alerted HTTPS activity (T246-00266, T246-00267, T246-00268, T246-00270).
Separate review: a proxy request for updates.paloaltonetworks.com with a GlobalProtect user agent received status 504; it is distinct from the repeated LedgerLink requests (T246-00045).
